extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers (interested in politics, military affairs, labor and housing policy)
extracted.subtask_description: Wire-service style newspaper reporting compiling datelined dispatches, eyewitness testimony excerpts, complete memoranda/speeches, and policy outlines on military hearings, labor disputes, and housing proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warning message delivery timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Col. Bratton states the message center would have messages 'encoded in three minutes, on the air in eight, and in the hands of the recipients in (I think) twenty.' He looked at his watch on delivering the message to the Signal Corps and the time was 11:50 A.M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these time benchmarks (encode: ~3 min; on-air: ~8 min; recipients: ~20 min) when assessing the timeliness and responsiveness of message handling and transmission; verify time stamps when reconstructing events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify critical reports before wider action
rubrics_metrics.description: When an enlisted man brought a pencil note saying 'Pearl Harbor attacked — This is no drill,' Marshall 'directed me to contact Hawaii if possible and verify the message.' Soon after, a more official message confirmed the first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an initial informal report is received, attempt rapid verification via direct contact with the receiving command before escalating; note whether subsequent 'official' confirmations arrived and their timestamps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give first priority to the Philippines (when priority unclear)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gen. Leonard T. Gerow (quoted) said: 'Tell them to give first priority to the Philippines' (or 'something to that effect'). Miles and others recalled urging that the Philippines receive first priority on the warning message.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When issuing simultaneous warnings to multiple overseas commands, decision-makers should explicitly assign priorities (e.g., Philippines first) and record the instruction and rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid alarming civilian population or disclosing intent
rubrics_metrics.description: Roosevelt's message advised: avoid public pronouncements or action 'since that might make the situation more difficult' and could 'alarm civil population or disclose intent.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft public or command messages to balance necessary warnings with operational security and civilian calm; explicitly consider wording that minimizes panic or disclosure of sensitive intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency (or documented justification for differences) of instructions across commands
rubrics_metrics.description: Lucas noted that instructions sent to commanding generals of the Caribbean defense command were identical with those which went to Short, but the Philippines received different instructions; this difference was highlighted as suspicious or noteworthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When commands receive different instructions in similar circumstances, document and justify the differences; treat identical instruction sets as a standard unless operational reasons dictate otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default secure-channel transmission and notification if otherwise
rubrics_metrics.description: Colonel Bratton stated the message center gave him no intimation that all four messages would not go over Army radio direct to the four Army headquarters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume secure Army radio/direct channel transmission as default for critical warnings; if alternative channels (commercial cables, etc.) are used, record and communicate that deviation and expected delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prescribed fact-finding procedure for major industrial disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: President Truman proposed legislation to create fact-finding commissions to inquire into major disputes; work stoppages would be barred while these boards operate (patterned 'after the Railway Labor act').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use fact-finding boards to investigate major labor disputes, with statutory or agreed temporary restrictions on strikes during their proceedings to facilitate unbiased fact-finding and possible settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Housing emergency lease and allocation terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal-agency outlines called for: (1) the states to maintain the property; (2) houses to be rented first to veterans and after that to the general public; (3) demountable houses in storage to be erected by the states on favorable federal sites; (4) leases to be for a maximum of five years with permission to terminate on six months' notice at the end of the housing emergency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design emergency housing programs with veterans-first allocation, state maintenance responsibility, use of demountable stock on federal sites, and time-limited leases (≤5 years) with six-month termination provisions post-emergency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convoy routing and zigzagging directives in dangerous waters
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions and basic documents provided that under certain conditions ships should sail a zigzag course in waters considered dangerous; however sailing orders for a specific voyage did not specify zigzagging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain standing directives requiring zigzagging in designated danger zones; ensure specific sailing orders reference or reaffirm standing security maneuvers to avoid ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Command responsibility to inquire about escort availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Lieut. Waldron testified that he checked with the area commander to inquire if an escort was available and was informed that one was not needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require commanding officers to confirm escort availability with higher command when planning voyages through possible submarine threat areas and to record the inquiry and response in sailing orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish complete texts of key memoranda and speeches for public record
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper reproduces 'the complete texts' of Major General Sherman Miles's memorandum and Philip Murray's radio address/speech in full.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When space allows, publishing full texts of important memoranda and speeches supports transparency and enables readers to see primary source wording rather than partial excerpts; label them clearly (e.g., 'Text of ...').

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline and source attribution in wire reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Items are presented with datelines (e.g., 'WASHINGTON, Dec. 4') and wire-service attribution (AP) at the top of dispatches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clear datelines and wire-service or reporter attribution to provide context about when and where a dispatch originated and the reporting source.
